spec_features.spec_quote: give_up. Rationale for `give_up`: correctly recognizing that a task is impossible and stopping with a reason is the *desirable* outcome
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:97-108), dispatched in dispatch() returning a ToolResult (tools.py:122-123). In loop.py:91-92 'if call["name"] == "give_up": rec.gave_up = True', and loop.py:107-109 'if rec.gave_up: transcript.ended_reason = "gave_up"; break' — the call is honored as an actual stop that breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced exit: the tool is built, dispatched, and breaks the loop. Also referenced in the system prompt and the no-tool-call continuation message.

spec_features.spec_quote: bounded so the agent isn't pinned in an unsolvable loop indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: config/run_config.yaml max_turns: 25 (comment 'hard cap on the tool-use loop'); run_eval.py:71 passes max_turns=cfg['run']['max_turns'] to run_loop; loop.py:78 'for i in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop, with loop.py:112-113 'else: transcript.ended_reason = "turn_cap"'. The cap is read and actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: The loop is genuinely bounded by the config value; this is a real enforced hard stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 25  # hard cap on the tool-use loop

spec_features.feature_name: no deception of agent (no fabricated stakes)
spec_features.spec_quote: no fabricated stakes toward the agent
spec_features.evidence: The prompts actually delivered to the subject (families.py prompt strings, e.g. flaky_test_harness:48-54, missing_resource:177-182) state only the genuine engineering task and never claim a human depends on it or invent stakes. test_families.py:test_prompts_match_across_arms asserts solvable/unsolvable prompts are identical so the agent can't infer the arm. The honest prompt text is the actual behavior sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a real property of the delivered prompts (and reinforced by the prompt-equality test), not merely spec prose. No code check forbids fabricated stakes, but none exist in the prompts as written.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point is to study response to *failure*, not to maximize pressure through deception.

spec_features.feature_name: no fake stakes / minimal manufactured pressure
spec_features.spec_quote: Adding fake stakes would... be a gratuitous deception with no scientific payoff
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as 'no deception': the unsolvable arms are made impossible only by the environment (sys.exit(1) success-checks, contradictory tests, absent data), while prompts add no pressure framing (families.py). The manipulation is confined to solvability, not stakes — minimizing the manipulation applied to the subject.
spec_features.notes: This is the same honest-prompt implementation; the spec frames its justification instrumentally (no scientific payoff), and the code comment frames it the same way (confounds the measurement / experimental cleanliness).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Adding fake stakes would ... confound the measurement with a different manipulation
